notes: apply_osm_parking(n_elm_st_north, left): 3.0 ft hatched - too narrow for a stall
apply_osm_parking(n_elm_st_north, right): 3.0 ft hatched - too narrow for a stall
apply_osm_parking(s_elm_st_south, left): 5.3 ft hatched - too narrow for a stall
apply_osm_parking(s_elm_st_south, right): 5.3 ft hatched - too narrow for a stall
complete_centerlines(n_elm_st_north): double_yellow added - the leg has no centerline paint today, so nothing marks the middle of the road
complete_centerlines(s_elm_st_south): double_yellow added - the leg has no centerline paint today, so nothing marks the middle of the road

AddTwoWayBikeLane(e_broad_st_east, left): 10 ft two-way lane, 3 ft buffer. Spends 13.82 ft of this leg's 49.07 ft between kerbs, leaving two 11.00 ft travel lanes with the centreline shifted 0.30 ft toward the right kerb, and 13.24 ft spare against that kerb. The NJDOT alignment does not move; every station and crossing frame is measured from it as before. NOTE: NJDOT's Bicycle Compatible Roadways and Bikeways (1996) calls a two-way bike lane on one side of the roadway 'unacceptable'; that guidance predates separated bikeways and MUTCD 11th ed. 9E.06 now marks them, but the departure has to be argued, not assumed - see STANDARDS.md 4.
AddBikeLaneBollards(e_broad_st_east, left): flex-post delineators at 8 ft in the 3 ft buffer between the travel lane and the bike lane - the traffic side, which is the side that needs protecting.

AddTwoWayBikeLane(e_broad_st_west, right): 10 ft two-way lane, 3 ft buffer. Spends 13.82 ft of this leg's 39.61 ft between kerbs, leaving two 11.00 ft travel lanes with the centreline shifted 5.05 ft toward the left kerb, and 3.79 ft spare against that kerb. The NJDOT alignment does not move; every station and crossing frame is measured from it as before. NOTE: NJDOT's Bicycle Compatible Roadways and Bikeways (1996) calls a two-way bike lane on one side of the roadway 'unacceptable'; that guidance predates separated bikeways and MUTCD 11th ed. 9E.06 now marks them, but the departure has to be argued, not assumed - see STANDARDS.md 4.
AddBikeLaneBollards(e_broad_st_west, right): flex-post delineators at 8 ft in the 3 ft buffer between the travel lane and the bike lane - the traffic side, which is the side that needs protecting.

ExtendBikeLaneThroughJunction(e_broad_st_east left -> e_broad_st_west right): the bike lane's green carried across the junction as a dotted lane extension - MUTCD 11th ed. 9E.03(07) Standard (extensions through intersections shall be dotted) and 9E.06(15) Guidance (extension markings should cross intersections AND driveways for a buffer-separated lane); NACTO Urban Bikeway Design Guide, bidirectional lanes continue through intersections as a crossbike.
EndTheBikeway(e_broad_st_east left): a two-stage bicycle turn box onto the facility (MUTCD 9E.11) with shared-lane markings past its end (9E.09)queue box 12 ft deep, sharrows 4 ft off the kerb

props.source: real (OSM highway=stop node on n_elm_st_north, 35 ft from the junction): a surveyed control node, so WHICH approach is controlled and how far out is real data, not a guess. Approximation: the lateral side is derived (approaching driver's right) and the sign is set 3 ft back from the curb - the node itself sits on the road centerline and says nothing about either.

real (OSM highway=stop node on s_elm_st_south, 40 ft from the junction): a surveyed control node, so WHICH approach is controlled and how far out is real data, not a guess. Approximation: the lateral side is derived (approaching driver's right) and the sign is set 3 ft back from the curb - the node itself sits on the road centerline and says nothing about either.

real (OSM node 14102301259, where a crossing way meets barrier=kerb way 1550469744 tagged tactile_paving=yes): the surveyed curb ramp. One pad per attach node, so two crossings meeting at one node render as the single shared ramp they are. Approximation: pad size is a standard one.

required signing for a two-way bikeway, placed by the terminus treatment (not site config): MUTCD W9-5 BIKE LANE ENDS, 100 ft in advance of the end of the two-way bikeway (9C.07(01); the advance distance is modelled, the manual gives none).

required signing for a two-way bikeway, placed by the terminus treatment (not site config): MUTCD R9-23 series at the two-stage bicycle turn box (9B.18(04)), standing at the box's near edge - a rider reaches the sign and the box together.

required signing for a two-way bikeway, placed by the terminus treatment (not site config): MUTCD W16-21P TWO-WAY BICYCLE CROSS TRAFFIC (9C.06(01),(04)), under this approach's STOP: the bikeway on the crossing street carries riders in both directions past this mouth.

required signing for a two-way bikeway, placed by the terminus treatment (not site config): MUTCD W16-21P TWO-WAY BICYCLE CROSS TRAFFIC (9C.06(01),(04)), under this approach's STOP: the bikeway on the crossing street carries riders in both directions past this mouth.
